Playbook.name: F5 WAF — Single Source Attacking Multiple Banking Applications - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: One source hit 2+ distinct banking application policies with high-rating (>=4) attacks. Triage question: is this a single actor systematically probing the bank's whole web estate (broad campaign), or shared infrastructure (NAT/proxy) aggregating unrelated traffic?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A source sweeping multiple banking apps is mapping the attack surface for the weakest entry point - an early, high-value warning.

Assets.AssetType: F5 BIG-IP ASM / Advanced WAF fronting JCB internet banking and public web apps
Published banking applications and their backend servers

LogSources.LogSource: F5 ASM CEF events via syslog -> logs-cef.log-* (observer.vendor F5)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: F5 ASM logging to CEF over syslog, parsed into logs-cef.log-* (verified live).

CEF fields: deviceCustomString4=attack_type, deviceCustomNumber2=violation_rating (>=4 = real attack), deviceCustomString1=security policy, requestUrl, requestMethod, deviceCustomNumber1=HTTP response code, deviceCustomString6=source geo, cef.name=violation name, event.action=passed|alerted|blocked.

Signal.Name: Cross-application attacker
Signal.Details: source.ip with high-rating attacks across cardinality(deviceCustomString1) >= 2.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Broad, methodical coverage of many apps from a single external IP is campaign behavior; a shared corporate NAT hitting apps its users legitimately use is not.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether one actor is systematically attacking multiple banking apps or the source is shared infrastructure.

Step.name: Per-application attack profile for this source
Step.Purpose: Show which apps, which attack types per app, and enforcement - a real campaign shows aggressive types across apps.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4 AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), attack_types = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4), passed = COUNT(CASE(event.action == "passed", 1, null)), blocked = COUNT(CASE(event.action == "blocked", 1, null)) BY cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1 | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Aggressive exploit types (SQLi/RFI/cmd-exec) across several policies = campaign. If each app shows only its own normal traffic pattern flagged benignly, suspect shared NAT.

Step.name: Timeline and breadth - methodical sweep vs bursty
Step.Purpose: A methodical sweep touches apps in sequence; shared NAT shows overlapping, continuous, mixed traffic.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS total = COUNT(*), apps = COUNT_DISTINCT(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1), high = COUNT(CASE(cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4, 1, null)), geo = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6), methods = VALUES(cef.extensions.requestMethod) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: High ratio of high-rating events to total, from a foreign geo, across many apps = campaign. Low high-rating ratio with huge total from an internal range = shared NAT/proxy noise.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows aggressive exploit types across 2+ apps from an external source (methodical coverage).
Node.Result: True Positive (Multi-Application Attack Campaign - escalate, watch for a successful breach on any app)

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows any app where events passed with backend responses (pivot to PB-F5-001 for that app).
Node.Result: True Positive (Campaign with Possible Reach - IR)

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows an internal shared-NAT source with a low high-rating ratio and normal per-app traffic.
Source is external and multi-app but the activity looks like a benign crawler/bot with occasional signature hits.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-F5MULTI-APPS, INV-02-F5MULTI-TIMING to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Shared infrastructure (corporate NAT/proxy) aggregating many users' legitimate traffic.

Indicators.Item: Low ratio of high-rating events to total.
Each app sees its own normal traffic.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the source is a NAT/proxy; consider XFF-based analysis.
Close as false_positive; tune if needed.

TruePositive.Definition: One actor systematically attacking multiple banking applications.

Indicators.Item: Aggressive exploit types across several apps.
Methodical coverage; any app where requests passed to backend.

SOCAction.Item: Escalate; block the source; review each targeted app.
Enforce blocking across the targeted policies; watch for a breach on the weakest app.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misassigned policy or shared VIP causing one source's traffic to appear across multiple app labels.

Indicators.Item: Apps share a VIP/policy mapping making attribution wrong.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Block the source if external campaign; list all targeted apps.
Prioritize any app that showed passed/backend reach.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Review each targeted app for compromise; enforce blocking; hunt the source's other activity.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Reduce shared-VIP ambiguity; enforce blocking on public banking apps; deploy bot defense.

QualityChecks.Check: Cardinality on deviceCustomString1 (policy) verified as the app discriminator.
XFF (deviceCustomString5) can refine attribution behind proxies.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Shared NAT confirmed; no methodical campaign; documented.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: All targeted apps reviewed; source blocked; no breach confirmed.
